extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

API 6A product specification level (PSL 1 to 4) sets the inspection, testing and traceability applied; PR1 and PR2 are the performance requirement levels, PR2 having passed API 6A design-validation testing. PSL 3G adds a gas test.

faqs.q: What is a cyclone desander for flowback used for?
faqs.a: Cyclone desanders for flowback: 5,000 to 20,000 psi, 2-1/16" to 4-1/16" ports, carbide cyclone elements, 200 L+ sand storage with continuous on-line discharge.

faqs.q: What do PSL 1 to 3G and PR1 mean on a cyclone desander?
faqs.a: PSL 1 to 3G is the product specification level range, where 3G adds a gas test, and PR1 is the performance requirement level. State the level you need on the RFQ.

faqs.q: What sizes and pressure ratings does the cyclone desander for flowback come in?
faqs.a: The listing covers 2-1/16" to 4-1/16" main and bypass ports nominal bore at 5,000 to 20,000 psi working pressure, with aPI 6A flanged or hammer union. Give the bore, working pressure and end connection on the enquiry and we match the exact model.

faqs.q: When should I choose a cyclone desander instead of a screen desander?
faqs.a: Choose the cyclone when sand loads are heavy, because it has no screen to plug and discharges sand continuously while staying on line. Choose the [double barrel screen desander](/p/double-barrel-screen-desander) for short-term clean-up and testing.

faqs.q: How is the cyclone desander for flowback tested?
faqs.a: For the cyclone desander for flowback (2-1/16" to 4-1/16" main and bypass ports, 5,000 to 20,000 psi working pressure): hydrostatic tests to API 6A / 16A / 16C at the PSL ordered, with function tests of valves and controls. The test record is supplied with the valve. Shell and seat tests are proof tests and are never working pressures.

faqs.q: Which material and temperature classes does the cyclone desander for flowback offer?
faqs.a: On the cyclone desander for flowback, body material is offered in API 6A material classes AA to HH (DD to HH for sour service), and the temperature range is -60 °C to 121 °C (K to V). For sour service the DD to HH classes apply to NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156. Give your temperature and H2S data on the enquiry.

faqs.q: Is the cyclone desander for flowback to API specification, and what documents are supplied?
faqs.a: The cyclone desander for flowback is built to API 6A (21st edition) by API-licensed manufacturers and supplied with the API certificate and monogram documentation. Material certificates, heat-treatment and NDE records and the test record come with it, and operator specifications are reviewed clause by clause.

faqs.q: How is the cyclone desander for flowback operated?
faqs.a: The cyclone desander for flowback is operated by manual, or remote with power choke. Operation is manual, or remote with a power choke. End connections on the listing are aPI 6A flanged or hammer union.

faqs.q: How does a cyclone desander remove sand from a flowback stream?
faqs.a: The well stream enters tangentially and spins, and centrifugal force throws sand to the wall, where it falls into a separate storage cylinder of 200 L or more and is discharged on line. Read the [well testing equipment guide](/blog/surface-well-testing-equipment).

faqs.q: Cyclone desander or double barrel screen desander for flowback?
faqs.a: A cyclone desander spins sand out by centrifugal force into a separate storage cylinder with no screen to plug, while a double-barrel screen desander holds sand on a screen and is emptied barrel by barrel. See the [Double Barrel Screen Desander, 5,000 to 20,000 psi](/p/double-barrel-screen-desander).
